prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every homeowner in Dallas — the right contractor depends on your budget, roof type, warranty needs, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and your location. Instead of one name, here’s a reliable way to find the best contractor for your job plus what to check for.

How to find the best roofing company in Dallas
- Search certified/endorsed contractors: use manufacturer locators (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) to find certified installers in Dallas — certification means extra training and better material warranties.  
- Read recent reviews: check Google, Yelp, and the BBB for recent projects and how they handled complaints.  
- Ask for references and photos of recent local jobs (same shingle type & slope).  
- Get at least 3 detailed written estimates to compare scope and materials.  
- Verify insurance and business credentials: general liability and worker’s comp insurance; local business registration and any city permits required.  
- Confirm warranties: materials warranty from the manufacturer and a workmanship/installation warranty from the contractor (get both in writing).  
- Check for storm-damage/insurance experience if applicable: if you’re using insurance, ask how they work with adjusters and whether they provide Xactimate-style estimates.

Key questions to ask every roofer
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Dallas and do you pull permits?  
- Are you insured? Can you provide certificates of liability and workers’ comp?  
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I want? (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster)  
- Who will do the work — your employees or subs? Will you provide lien waivers?  
- What’s the estimated start/completion date, and what’s the payment schedule? (Avoid large upfront cash payments.)  
- What cleanup and disposal will you do? Will you protect landscaping?  
- What warranties are provided, and how are warranty claims handled?

Red flags
- No written estimate or contract.  
- Requests for full payment or very large deposit up front.  
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide certificate.  
- No physical business address or poor/old online reviews with unresolved complaints.  
- High-pressure sales tactics or “storm chaser” behavior (appears only after storms).

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated roofing contractors near your address or zip code and give a short vetted list, or  
- Review 2–3 quotes/estimates you get and point out differences and potential issues.

Tell me your zip code or share the estimates and I’ll help find and compare reputable Dallas roofers.
